name: Client data layer
purpose: Owns server-state caching, request lifecycle, invalidation, optimistic updates, and offline queueing; the seam between the UI and the wire.
responsibilities: Maintain the server-state cache with stale-while-revalidate reads and explicit invalidation on writes (application-spa-REQ-013).
Expose per-query status (loading, error, success, empty) that routes and components bind their state quartet to (application-spa-REQ-010).
Detect network loss, surface it to the shell banner, queue or refuse writes per policy, and replay on reconnect (application-spa-REQ-014).
Normalise wire errors into the problem-details envelope shape declared in ADR-204-application-spa-error-envelope before they reach UI code.
Attach session credentials and handle 401 responses by routing through the session-expiry flow (application-spa-REQ-009).
internalStructure: A query/mutation layer with a keyed cache; keys derive from the canonical URL shapes in application-spa-REQ-001 so invalidation maps one-to-one to resources.

dependencies.name: Error envelope decision
dependencies.description: ADR-204-application-spa-error-envelope; the application-api-rest blueprint contributes the server half of the same topic.

tradeoffs: A dedicated data layer costs indirection on trivial fetches and buys one place to verify caching, invalidation, offline, and auth behaviour instead of per-screen re-implementations.
